relevance_rank_note: PhD thesis (Li 2026, Oxford) with isogenic APOE3/APOE4 human iPSC astrocyte pairs from three donors (one control, two sporadic AD), endogenous APOE. In astrocyte monoculture, EEA1 staining intensity is higher in APOE4. High-content imaging, intensity only (no endosome size for astrocytes); unreviewed, figure-read values.

quote: In monoculture, APOE4 astrocytes consistently exhibited lower nuclear intensity and reduced endosome roundness, but increased cytoplasmic width-to-length ratio, higher BODIPY intensity, and higher EEA1 intensity compared to APOE3 astrocytes.
system: Isogenic APOE3 and APOE4 human iPSC astrocytes (lentiviral NFIB induction) from three donors: control donor 1 (AG09173, female), sAD donor 1 (UKBi011-A, male), sAD donor 2. Endogenous APOE, astrocyte monoculture without Abeta, EEA1 immunostaining, high-content imaging with Harmony feature extraction, two-way ANOVA (genotype x Abeta). Pooled panel of all three donors.
description: Early-endosome marker EEA1 staining was brighter in isogenic APOE4 human iPSC astrocytes than APOE3 (three donors pooled): about 625 vs 570 FU, about 10% higher, p < 0.0001 (significant in two of three donors separately).
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4, isogenic human iPSC astrocytes, 3 donors) -> (higher EEA1 intensity)
location: Thesis Fig. 6.12 I4 (PDF page 209), no-Abeta bars
human_check: Unreviewed DPhil thesis (University of Oxford, 2026), so source type Other. Effect and p read from the figure (**** bracket). Dots appear to be wells or fields pooled across donors, so p probably reflects technical replicates; n not stated. The thesis text names different significant donors in two places (I1/I3 vs I2/I3); the figure shows I1 and I3 with brackets. EEA1 intensity is a staining amount, not endosome size or recycling, so class 3 and strength 5. Two of the three donors have sporadic AD (iPSC lines, not aged tissue). The roundness panel (J4) shows APOE4 slightly higher, opposite to the text; no row.
